subject: Chemistry
title: The Light Thief: Why Transition-Metal Ions Are Coloured
summary: Ligands split the five d orbitals of a transition-metal ion into a lower and an upper level. A d electron absorbs the one band of visible light whose energy equals the gap and jumps up (a d–d transition); the rest of the light reaches the eye, so we see the complementary colour: Ti³⁺(aq) eats green-yellow and looks purple, Cu²⁺(aq) eats red-orange and looks blue. The ligand sets the gap (ruby and emerald are both Cr³⁺), and d⁰ / d¹⁰ ions such as Sc³⁺ and Zn²⁺ are colourless.

notes.title: 10 – Formation of Coloured Ions: Why Transition-Metal Ions Are Coloured

keyPoints: Ligands split the five d orbitals into a **lower and an upper level** with a small energy gap.
A d electron absorbs light whose **energy equals the gap** and jumps up: a **d–d transition**, usually in the visible region.
We see the **complementary colour** of the light absorbed: Ti³⁺ absorbs green-yellow → purple; Cu²⁺ absorbs red-orange → blue.
The **ligand sets the gap** (same Cr³⁺: ruby red, emerald green); **d⁰ and d¹⁰** ions (Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺, Zn²⁺) are colourless.

blocks.p: Complementary colours sit opposite each other on a colour wheel.

Ti³⁺ (3d¹) in water absorbs light near 500 nm (green-yellow) as its one d electron jumps to the upper level; red and blue are transmitted, so [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is **purple**. Ti⁴⁺ (3d⁰) has no d electron and is colourless.

quiz.q: The colour of most transition-metal ions is due to:
quiz.explain: A d electron jumps from a lower to a higher d level by absorbing visible light.

options: the complementary colour of the light absorbed
quiz.explain: The transmitted (unabsorbed) light reaches the eye.
Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰: no d electron to jump.

quiz.q: Zn²⁺ salts are colourless because Zn²⁺ is:
quiz.explain: All d orbitals are full: no vacancy above, no d–d transition.

quiz.q: Ti³⁺(aq) absorbs green-yellow light. It looks:
quiz.explain: Red and blue are left: purple (NCERT Table 4.8).

quiz.q: Cu²⁺(aq) is blue because it absorbs:
quiz.explain: Blue is the complementary colour that is transmitted.

quiz.q: The frequency of light absorbed by a transition-metal ion is decided mainly by:
quiz.explain: NCERT 4.3.10: the ligand sets the size of the d-orbital splitting.

quiz.q: Ruby and emerald are both coloured by Cr³⁺. Their colours differ because:
options: the d-orbital gap differs in their surroundings
quiz.explain: Ruby's gap is larger (absorbs yellow-green → red); emerald's smaller (absorbs red-orange → green).

quiz.q: Which pair has only coloured ions in water?
quiz.explain: Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) green and Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) pink both have partly filled d orbitals.

quiz.q: In a free (isolated) gaseous ion the five d orbitals:
quiz.explain: Ligands are needed to split them.

simulation.reason: The idea is a qualitative chain (split levels → one band absorbed → complementary colour; d⁰/d¹⁰ colourless) over a fixed table of ions; the video, memory cards, colour table and 25 workbook questions teach it fully, and there is no continuous variable a student would usefully change.
